literal: Ruin-without supreme-wealth learning to-a-person; wealth are-not other those.
translation: Learning is the indestructible, supreme wealth for a person; all other possessions are not true wealth.
modern: ஒருவனுக்கு அழிவில்லாத சிறந்த செல்வம் கல்வியே ஆகும்; அதைத் தவிர மற்றவை எல்லாம் உண்மையான செல்வம் அல்ல.
explanation: This couplet establishes education as the ultimate human possession. The poet describes learning as 'viḻuccelvam' (supreme wealth) because it is 'kēṭil' (without ruin or decay), unlike material riches which can be lost, stolen, or spent. The word 'māṭu' is used here in its classical sense of 'wealth' or 'property'. By declaring that all other things are not true wealth, the verse emphasizes that intellectual and moral growth through education is the only permanent asset a person can acquire.
